3_template_alignment_train_vs_gguf.evidence: reports/epoch-2/production/gates/qwen_template_alignment.json. gen_prompt is an exact prefix of the training text, assistant content follows it, markers occur exactly once each, and gguf_render_equals_hf_render is true.
3_template_alignment_train_vs_gguf.note_on_string_inequality: gguf_template_equals_hf_template is FALSE while gguf_render_equals_hf_render is TRUE -- the embedded template text differs but produces byte-identical output. The gate's pass condition requires render equality, not string equality (gemma had the same profile in epoch-1).
3_template_alignment_train_vs_gguf.first_attempt_was_a_false_failure: an initial run without --template-kwargs reported FAIL. That was the harness, not the model: with no kwargs the generation prompt renders in THINKING mode (open <think>) while the training text renders the closed empty block, so they cannot match. Re-run with enable_thinking=false -- the setting the eval path already uses -- it passes. Recorded because a bare FAIL in the log would otherwise look like a real alignment defect.
3_template_alignment_train_vs_gguf.independent_confirmation: verified separately without any GGUF: to_text() training render and the eval-time generation prompt (enable_thinking=False) agree exactly, gen_prompt is an exact prefix, assistant content follows. Qwen's template emits the closed <think></think> prefix in the training render by default, so training and inference agree with no --template-kwargs at training time, exactly as in epoch-1.

4_native_fit_no_sysmem_spill.status: PASS expected -- and Qwen is the only architecture with real headroom
4_native_fit_no_sysmem_spill.evidence: epoch-1 qwen-v2 measured 10.8 GiB allocated / 18.0 GiB reserved against a 23.889 GiB ceiling -- 5.9 GiB of headroom, the only one of the six that never approached the limit. That is a real measurement at the identical configuration.
4_native_fit_no_sysmem_spill.why_not_probe_based: the 12-step probe reports 10.3/13.1 GiB. Both prior probes underpredicted badly (granite probe 16.9 vs 24.6 actual; phi probe 10.8 vs 28.4 actual), so the probe was used only to confirm the trainable count and step time. The memory judgement rests on epoch-1's measured value.
4_native_fit_no_sysmem_spill.caveat_from_phi: phi's epoch-2 reserved memory rose 26.3 -> 28.4 GiB versus epoch-1 at identical config, so reserved CAN drift upward with run length once a model is already spilling. Qwen starts 5.9 GiB under the ceiling, so even a comparable drift should stay native. Not asserted as certain -- the full training log is the authoritative record.
